# Kid journey round 2: Caleb's notes on mockup direction A (Oct 22, 2026)

Caleb picked direction A (`docs/design/kid-journey-mockups/`, canvas 1FXGT2LF6xteKtyeUMTzjq) and asked for it built
straight into the app. **The rule above everything, in his words: "DECLUTTER DECLUTTER DECLUTTER. This is
non-negotiable. Any section that just has too many words must be reduced. I don't care if we have to cut features;
prioritize clarity, intuition and accessibility of core features."**

Answers he gave in follow-up questions:
- Build straight into the app (no second mockup round).
- Home preview: "almost like a fanned-out deck, or a visual similar to a recipe book (most scalable, works regardless
  of how many dishes there are, don't need to worry about spacing the boxes)".
- Numbered circles: solid dark green fill, light green number.
- Short substeps: rewritten short once per recipe (Gemini) and stored in the recipe data.

## His 14 notes (lightly edited for reading)

**Home.** Home is a portal: the first thing you see, and from it you can get anywhere. No recommended dish. Instead a
sneak peek into the recipes (the deck), and a "Start cooking" button under it that goes to the Recipes tab. Under that,
a second button for the second reason people open the app: "Have a question about a dish?" The path is: pick the dish,
pick the person to ask, land in that chat. That is the entire Home page. It frees up the space "Cook this" and
"More dishes" took.

1. (Home, above.)
2. Recipe overview (A): good overall; showing all the steps up front is liked. Invert the numbered circles (green
   circle, lighter green number). Ingredients: cut the quotes under them ("one good one about as long as my forearm",
   "head on", "a good rub all over", "a pinch for the sauce later"...). Just the measurement and the ingredient.
3. Recorded recipe overview (13 steps): good. Same: invert the circles; steps, measurement and ingredient only.
4. Recorded step 1 ("Preheat the pan"): invert the circles. Sub-instructions very short: two lines at most, then
   "..." and tap to drop down more detail. Should look a lot more decluttered.
5. The video goes above "Hear Miles": most kids were drawn to the video first.
6. The video goes above all the substeps (e.g. "Mix the miso glaze"); it was the most helpful thing.
7. Option to expand the video to full screen, and also to watch it inline without full screen.
8. Every substep at most two lines. Declutter.
9. The full-screen video view looks good.
10. Messaging: not the mockup's horizontal people row. Copy Instagram's structure: chats listed vertically with the
    last message visible in each.
11. (Cooking step 1, the fish.)
12. "Dad's tip" should be a collapsed pill with a down arrow you tap to drop it down. It adds too much clutter open.
13. In a step, make it clear exactly which ingredients that step needs.
14. Cut placeholders like "Rub amount: ask Dad". Rename "You need" to "Ingredients" (or a short "This step's
    ingredients").
